title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
oneLinerQuestion: Find the kth smallest value in a Binary Search Tree using inorder property.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Kth Smallest Element in a BST problem requires finding the kth smallest numerical value (1-indexed) in a Binary Search Tree. By definition of a BST, all elements in a node's left subtree are strictly smaller, and all elements in its right subtree are strictly greater. Consequently, an in-order traversal (Left -> Node -> Right) visits nodes in strictly sorted, ascending order. Rather than traversing the entire tree or dumping all values into an auxiliary array, we can use an iterative in-order traversal with an explicit stack. Drilling down to the leftmost leaf and popping nodes one by one yields elements from smallest to largest; maintaining an extraction counter lets us terminate and return immediately the moment the kth node is popped, avoiding unnecessary traversals of the remaining tree.

- Step 1: Auxiliary Stack & State Tracking — We initialize an empty stack `stack = []` to store ancestor node references during descent, an active node pointer `curr = root`, and a counter `n = 0` to track the count of processed elements in ascending order.

- Step 2: In-Order Traversal Loop Guard — We execute a while loop `while (curr !== null || stack.length > 0)` that continues until all nodes have been explored or our early termination condition is met.

- Step 3: Drilling Down the Left Subtree — While `curr !== null`, we push `curr` onto the stack (`stack.push(curr)`) and advance strictly along the left link (`curr = curr.left`). This continues until `curr` reaches `null`, positioning the smallest available element at the top of the stack.

- Step 4: Popping the Minimum Available Node — We pop the topmost element from the stack: `curr = stack.pop()`. This is the next smallest element in the global BST order.

- Step 5: Counter Evaluation & Early Return — We increment our counter: `n++`. We then check: `if (n === k) return curr.val`. When `n` matches `k`, the popped node is guaranteed to be the kth smallest element in the tree, allowing immediate return without touching the rest of the tree.

- Step 6: Advancing to Right Subtree — If `n !== k`, we move to explore the right branch of the current node: `curr = curr.right`. The outer while loop restarts, drilling down into the left branch of this new right child.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(H + k) where H is the tree height; in the best case for small k, the algorithm finishes in O(k) steps without visiting all N nodes (worst case O(N) for a skewed tree where k is near the end). Space Complexity: O(H) auxiliary space to maintain the explicit stack holding at most the height of the tree (O(log N) for balanced trees, O(N) for degenerate trees).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION kthSmallest(root, k):
    stack = EMPTY_STACK(), curr = root, n = 0
    WHILE curr IS NOT NULL OR NOT IS_EMPTY(stack) DO:
        WHILE curr IS NOT NULL DO PUSH curr TO stack; curr = curr.left
        curr = POP(stack); n = n + 1
        IF n == k THEN RETURN curr.val
        curr = curr.right
    END WHILE
END FUNCTION
